observation.visible_scene: On a flat white surface, a left hand grips a reflective metallic spherical puzzle ball (with a visible equatorial seam), while a loose scatter of small metallic jigsaw-shaped pieces lies in the center. A right hand enters from the upper right holding several of the same pieces.
visible_changes: The right hand, palm up, lets its held pieces slip off one after another onto the central pile (frames 1-6), reducing to a single piece.
The right hand then pinches and repositions that last piece and drops it (frames 9-14).
The right hand withdraws out of the top-right of the frame and is gone by frame 16, leaving only the left hand and the sphere.

The left hand keeps its grip on the sphere but slowly rotates/turns it (frames 23-41); as it turns, the seam tilts and the surface reveals metallic puzzle pieces already adhered to the ball together with empty gaps where pieces are missing.
The central pile of scattered pieces grows slightly during the drops and then remains static; the left hand and sphere stay in roughly the same left-side position throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the right hand does after leaving the frame, and whether it returns.
How or when the pieces became attached to the sphere, and whether the ball is being assembled, demonstrated, or just displayed.
The state of the scene before t=0 (the pieces were already in the right hand at the first frame).
uncertain_details: Whether the pieces on the sphere are magnetically fixed or merely resting; the clip shows them staying on during rotation but does not reveal the mechanism.
Camera motion is minimal/uncertain; the background stays consistent, so apparent sphere movement is attributed to the left hand turning it rather than to camera movement.
Reflections on the sphere (room, hand, camera) are surface reflections, not separate objects.
